name: bluebird-promisifyall-multiargs-wary
behavioral_change: In bluebird v_new (3.0.0), `Promise.promisify` and `Promise.promisifyAll` by default resolve the promise with only the first success value passed to the node-style callback, whereas v_old (2.x) collected multiple success values into an array. The call form is unchanged and no exception is raised by the library itself; the old array behaviour is restored with the new `multiArgs: true` option.
downstream_effect: wary's lib/temporal.coffee promisifies the `tmp` module and consumes `tmp.fileAsync().spread (temporalPath) ->`; after the upgrade the promise resolves to the path string, `.spread` iterates it character by character, `temporalPath` becomes `/`, and `fs.copySync` fails with `EISDIR` and `EACCES`. The output never mentions bluebird options, promisify or multiArgs; stack frames do name lib/temporal.coffee:54 (the `fs.copySync` call), which is the right file but a different line from the `promisifyAll` call on line 27 that must be edited.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in lib/temporal.coffee, adding `multiArgs: true` to the `Promise.promisifyAll(require('tmp'))` call on line 27.
documented_in: bluebird's "New in bluebird 3.0" document (docs/docs/new-in-bluebird-3.md, tag v3.7.2), section Promisification API changes, states in prose that promisification now uses only the first callback argument and that a new boolean option `multiArgs` restores the array behaviour. The document gives only prose for this change and no code showing `Promise.promisifyAll(fn, {multiArgs: true})`.

Temporal: .fromFile() given a file should be a copy of the file
